note: The external-dependency registry: the capabilities this repository NEEDS
This file is the ENUMERATION. The entry shape it must satisfy lives in
reads that schema's field lists rather than restating them — one carrier,
so amending the contract is one edit and never a two-copy divergence.
An unmet dependency is REPORTED, never gated (SPEC.md §5). The check fails
on a malformed or incomplete entry and never on a world that currently
fails to satisfy one: whether a setting elsewhere is flipped is a fact
about the world outside this repository, which changes without anyone
A capability an act depended on and this list of dependencies did not
declare is recorded there REPORT-ONLY WITH ITS REASON, never silently
admitted. Nothing in this repository detects such an observation
mechanically today — entries are written by hand when a run meets one —
and that gap is stated in the check's own output rather than left to be

dependencies.capability: the `allow_auto_merge` setting enabled on the GitHub repository tim-nish/kogaki
needed_by: enabling auto-merge on a pull request (`gh pr merge --auto`), which the ship lane uses to hand a converged PR to the branch-protection gates rather than merging it by hand
the held-run remedy of kogaki#55: a lane that intends to arm auto-merge and finds the repository setting off

verification.answers: is auto-merge enabled on this repository? the call prints `true` or `false`

dependencies.absence_signature: `gh pr merge --auto` exits non-zero with "Auto-merge is not allowed for this repository", and a lane that does not read that exit reports the PR as handed off while nothing is armed — the stall presents as a PR that simply never merges

dependencies.capability: the merge-eligibility PreToolUse deny installed in the actor's own Claude Code settings (`~/.claude/settings.json`), written by `~/.claude/tools/story-sync install-hooks`
needed_by: the merge-eligibility rule's enforcement half — the deny is what refuses a `gh pr merge` that no approved-closes receipt covers
any lane that treats the merge layer as guarded rather than as advice; with the hook uninstalled the rule is a document nobody is required to read

verification.command: grep -q lint-pr-merge "$HOME/.claude/settings.json" 2>/dev/null && echo true || echo false
verification.answers: does the actor's settings file register the merge-eligibility PreToolUse hook? the read prints `true` or `false`

dependencies.absence_signature: an ineligible `gh pr merge` runs to completion and merges — nothing refuses it and nothing logs the refusal that did not happen, so the enforcement gap is visible only in the merged result, which looks exactly like an eligible merge

dependencies.capability: the tool grants a spawned reviewer session actually receives from its host (the MCP servers, Bash and file tools available inside the session the review lane starts — the engine's, since kogaki#630)
needed_by: the review lane's spawned reviewer, which cannot produce a report without the tools that read the diff and post it. NOTE (kogaki#630): the spawner is claude-toolkit's engine, not this repository — kogaki retired its own sweep, so this dependency is needed BY an act kogaki no longer performs and FOR a session the engine still spawns against kogaki PRs
any consultation the spawned session is expected to perform, which needs the gateway tool to be granted inside that session rather than in the spawning one

verification.reason: the grant set belongs to a session that does not exist until it is spawned, and the host exposes no read of what a future session will be granted — the only way to learn it is to spawn a session and observe what it could do, which is the act this read would have preceded. kogaki#60 declares the grant-list contract; until a host-side read exists this stays a typed `none`, which is evidence, rather than an omission, which is not

dependencies.absence_signature: the spawned session completes blocked at the permission wall and exits report-less — the sweep records a spawn and no report, which is indistinguishable at read time from a reviewer that found nothing to say

observed_non_members.capability: the `Edit` tool inside a spawned REVIEW session (`REVIEW_TOOLS`, tools/review-sweep.sh)
observed_non_members.reason: Met undeclared on 2026-08-09: PR #313's round-1 reviewer was denied `Edit`, exited 1 and produced NO report — one owner grant and one of the two rounds SPEC.md §4 clause 3 allows, spent for nothing. Confirmed by headless probe under the same allowlist. Cause was a role asymmetry inside one file: the FIX role held `Edit` and the REVIEW role did not, while both already held `Write`. GRANTED under kogaki#310 (owner selection 2026-08-09); recorded here because the fallback records what an act depended on and the enumeration did not declare, whether or not the enumeration is later widened.

observed_non_members.capability: removing a file inside the spawned session's OWN worktree (`Bash(rm ...)`)
observed_non_members.reason: Met undeclared on 2026-08-09: PR #312's reviewer was denied `rm -f /tmp/kogaki-review-312-.../tree/.review-312-report.md` while cleaning up its own scratch report. Confirmed by headless probe. NOT granted and deliberately so — the sweep removes the worktree itself, so the capability is unnecessary rather than merely ungranted; recorded report-only per SPEC.md §4 so the absence is disclosed rather than silent.

observed_non_members.capability: a legible refusal label for a PIPED command (`denied_tools()` reports the LEADING command)
observed_non_members.reason: Met undeclared on 2026-08-09: PR #312's session recorded a denial labelled `Bash(gh pr view)`, a shape that IS granted — the refused member was elsewhere in a pipe. Not a missing capability but a missing PROPERTY of the denial record, and it belongs here because it is what made the other two observations hard to read. NOT repaired: kogaki#310 AC 6 declines re-cutting terminal_key(), whose three-word width is load-bearing for the PreToolUse gate and was chosen against measured failure in both directions.

observed_non_members.capability: a leading shell `grep` carrying an `-E` regex with an alternation and a quantifier (e.g. `grep -nE '^#{1,3} |trigger terms' <file>`)
observed_non_members.reason: Met undeclared on 2026-08-09: PR #322's round-2 reviewer was refused this shape while the SAME session successfully ran `grep -n '<simple>' <file>`. Reproduced in fresh sessions with no PreToolUse gate installed: `grep -n 'h2'`, `grep -n '#'`, `grep -c beta` and `<granted> | grep -c .` all ran; `grep -nE '^#{1,3} |text'` and `grep -nE '^t{1,3} |text'` were both refused — so `#` is NOT the discriminator and the terminal-key gate is ruled out (its store is per-spawn and was empty). NOT granted: the discriminating rule lives in the harness's own command parser, which this repository cannot read, so which shapes to enumerate is undecidable from here. Recorded report-only per SPEC.md §4; the open question is carried at kogaki#324.

observed_non_members.capability: `Bash(timeout ...)` as a leading command wrapping a granted one (e.g. `timeout 300 bash tools/review-sweep.sh ...`)
observed_non_members.reason: Met undeclared on 2026-08-09: PR #321's round-2 reviewer wrapped a granted `bash tools/...` invocation in `timeout 300` and was refused, the label naming `Bash(timeout 300 bash)` — correctly, since `terminal_key` takes the first three words and `timeout` is the leading command. NOT granted and deliberately so: a reviewer bounding its own commands is reasonable, but granting a wrapper widens every shape it can wrap, which is the enumeration-growth polarity kogaki#74 warns against. The reviewer's remedy is to invoke the granted form directly.
